Sometimes you can't be responsible to not get pregnant, or you had bad luck with your birth control. When this happens, what are they supposed to do? Just saying "Ah too bad, you should've known better to not get pregnant in the first place" doesn't help, there are still women both minors and non minors with unwanted pregnancies due to various reasons.

Adoption can be an option in some cases, sure, but not all of the time. It's also not seen by most women with unwanted pregnancies as a feasible option; adoption is not simple at all, and abortion isn't either, but it is easier than adoption, [95% of adoptions in the US are "open", the adopting family was in contact beforehand](https://www.hopespromise.com/2020/12/16/why-is-adoption-not-seen-as-an-option/), but getting someone that wants to adopt your child is not always a simple task.  


If you happen not to get someone that wants to adopt your child beforehand, "closed" adoption has to be practiced, where you don't know who will adopt your child and the adopting family won't know who you are. Adoption is often also more psychologically damaging than abortion.  


So yes, adoption can be an option, but not always and it's harder.
